concerns.issue: The article setting the score is speculative and unverifiable: the headline reports only that Boeing 'leaves open possibility' of more layoffs, and the retrieved article body is identical to the headline with no supporting text. It is nonetheless scored severity 4 (base 80.0, decayed 79.5), the same severity as the confirmed cut in GN-8b3ff62ef798. A conditional non-event should not carry the same weight as an executed action. The band does not depend on this item, but the headline score of 27.8 is inflated by it.

The payment input carries 65% of the weight yet the review itself flags trend as 'insufficient_history'. The entire record is one $650k invoice resolved 3 days late, from a single policyholder, against one $9M accepted line last reviewed April 2026. The formula treats this thin file as a clean 0.0 DPD score; it is more accurately an absence of data than demonstrated good payment behaviour, so the 0.0 input is low-confidence in both directions.

Material credit-positive evidence is scored 0.0 and cannot offset negative signal. A $745B backlog (GN-7504c72f4e2d), the uncontested $20B F/A-XX Navy award (GN-adc7305ae61d), a $12B aircraft sale (GN-ceb9c0f6ce22) and FAA clearance of the 737 Max software glitch (GN-04517ee3f157) all speak directly to forward revenue and ability to pay. The one-sided construction means the score reflects adverse news flow rather than net credit position.

Conversely, the formula appears to use only the single worst article, so the persistent production-constraint cluster never aggregates: 737 Max ramp-up deferred to late 2027 (GN-bd48ec482082, severity 2), Max 10 certification delayed (GN-dccc8a1c0d90, severity 2) and the FAA oversight audit (GN-4d5a109d9bdd, severity 2) contribute nothing beyond the top item. This is the more durable risk theme and is arguably under-weighted even as the speculative layoff headline is over-weighted.
